title: The Plot And Devastation Of Gaza In The Bible | Part 2

sense.text:
God gives you the name of the people that took the land: “Idumea, which have appointed my land into their possession”. Remember, the Arabs were there prior to them. Write this down: the Ottoman Turks took the land during the time of the Middle Ages, then the Arabs came in, and then Idumea came in with Britain.

“With the joy of all their heart”: they were happy to take the land; they have always wanted God’s holy land. And they didn’t go in as Idumeans. They said, no, we can’t go in as Idumeans, we’ve got to go in as the people of God: ‘I am Jew, I am Jewish.’ That is what “the joy of all their heart” means.

“With despiteful minds”: they took the land despite knowing that they were not the people of God, the Jews, and despite knowing that the land is not theirs.

“To cast it out for a prey”: they told their fellow Europeans to prey on the land. They told the British, come get a piece of the land as Jewish, British Jews, come get a piece of the land; my Jewish brethren from Poland, from Germany, from Czechoslovakia, from Uzbekistan, from Russia, from America, from Australia, come get a piece of this land.
Now the Lord says to us, “Prophesy therefore concerning the land of Israel”. God is telling you the land has “borne the shame of the heathen.” So who’s in the land? The heathen.
“Surely the heathen that are about you, they shall bear their shame.” The shame is going to come on the people in the land, in God’s holy land and our motherland.

Write this down: “the king of the south” is Egypt.

“Also the robbers of thy people”: the robbers of our people are the same people that robbed our land and robbed our identity. They “exalt themselves” as the Jews, and they exalted themselves “to establish the vision”: the vision that the land is theirs, that it is their land.

“But they shall fall.” Do you all hear the prophecy, brothers? They shall fall. They want us to believe that the land is theirs, they want us to believe that they’re the Jews. They’re not the Jews; you’re the Jews. It said they would take the land, and they took our identity.

“And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.” This is the taking of the land. And what is God’s heritage? Joel 3:2 gives the name of it: Israel. So “even a man and his heritage” is Israel.

precepts.why:
Joel gives the name of God’s heritage: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel”. See, God’s heritage is Israel.

So when Micah says they oppress “a man and his heritage”, the heritage that was taken by violence is Israel, the people and the land of God.

sense.text:
Here’s the evidence, here’s the proof. Christ says to the real Israelites, “I know thy works, and tribulation”: I know the hell you catch. “And poverty”: I know your poverty, “but thou art rich”. Why? Because all the promises in the Bible pertain to us.

“And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” That ain’t coming from us; that’s coming from the Son of God, the real Jew himself, the King of kings and the Lord of lords. He says they are not the Jews.

Christ is telling you that his brothers, the Jews, are you: you so-called blacks and Hispanics and Native American Indians. These people that are calling themselves Jews are not Christ’s brothers. They are not the Jews that the Bible is talking about. They are the impostors.

“Hear the counsel of the Lord”: it means hear the Bible. The Bible is the counsel of the Lord, “that he hath taken against Edom”. Who is Edom, brothers? This so-called white man. Idumea is the same race of people.

“Surely the least of the flock”: think about all of Edom. You’ve got America, Britain, Germany, France, Russia, Poland, Australia, South Africa. And the least of the flock, especially in the Middle East, is the so-called Israelis. They’re like a blip on the screen compared to everybody else. Three quarters of the earth are black and brown, one quarter is Esau, and the smallest of all of Edom is the so-called Israelis.

“Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock shall draw Edom out. Those people over there that call themselves the Israelites are the least of the flock, and they’re the ones that are going to draw the nations to war. “Surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall”. Remember what we read in Daniel 11:14: they exalt themselves to establish the vision, but they shall fall.

“The noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.” The Red Sea is over there in the Middle East. So it is telling you that what is going to draw them out is the land of Israel, and they shall fall.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle”. Who’s the eagle, brothers? Edom, the United States of America. The United States will come to help, as an eagle comes.

“And spread his wings over Bozrah”: write this down, Bozrah was the capital city of Edom, and it is in modern-day Jordan.

“And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” They’re going to fall; they’re going to be like a woman in pain. America is going to try to help, to no avail. That’s the prophecy.

The next question: what in the world is going on in Palestine today? One word, brothers: prophecy. We’ve gone over Isaiah 14 for a long time now, and we see things coming to fruition. “Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand”.

“That I will break the Assyrian in my land”. When you read about the Assyrian captivity, they took the northern kingdom of Israel out and put transplants in. The transplants it is talking about here are Idumea, the so-called white man. It’s a metaphor, a similitude: God will break the Idumeans in his land, “and upon my mountains tread him under foot”.

“Then shall his yoke depart from off them”. Write this down: the them is the Palestinians, and the yoke is a police state. “And his burden depart from off their shoulders”: his burden is the same as the yoke, a police state.

“This is the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth: and this is the hand that is stretched out upon all the nations.” God’s purpose is to tread Edom, Idumea, under foot and destroy them.

“For the Lord of hosts hath purposed, and who shall disannul it?” Who can change what God has spoken? “And his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?” Who shall turn back the hand of God?
“In the year that king Ahaz died was this burden.” That is when Isaiah saw that vision, that prophecy.

“Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina”: that’s the proof that the them in verse 25 is the Palestinians. Why would they rejoice? “Because the rod of him that smote thee is broken”: because the power of Idumea is broken. And God told the Palestinians, don’t you rejoice, because the land ain’t yours either.

“And his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent”: a fiery flying serpent is missiles.

“And the firstborn of the poor shall feed”: that’s Israel, that’s us; we’re going to feed. “And the needy shall lie down in safety”: we are the needy, and we’re going to lie down in safety. Why? Because Idumea is trodden under foot and the Palestinians are taken down as well.

“And I will kill thy root with famine, and he shall slay thy remnant”: that’s the Idumeans and the Palestinians.

“Howl, O gate; cry, O city; thou, whole Palestina, art dissolved”. The Lord is saying, I’m not finished with you Palestinians. Dissolved: they’re going to be erased out of the land.

“For there shall come from the north a smoke”: the north is North America, and they’re going to send a missile. “And none shall be alone in his appointed times”: when that missile hits.
“The poor of his people shall trust in it”: the poor of God’s people, Zion, shall trust in his holy word.

precepts.why:
The firstborn of the poor is us. Here is the precept: “Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”.

So when Isaiah says “the firstborn of the poor shall feed, and the needy shall lie down in safety”, that is Israel, God’s firstborn, the needy, who will feed and lie down in safety when Idumea is trodden under foot.

sense.text:
“The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines”. What’s the modern-day word for the Philistines, brothers? Palestine. “Before that Pharaoh smote Gaza.”

Some people jump up and say, ‘Y’all can’t use those scriptures, that stuff already happened once already.’ But 2 Esdras 5:42 shows God’s judgment is like a ring: it keeps on going.

Now the question is Pharaoh. There are no pharaohs in the land right now. Who’s the Pharaoh of today? Romans 9 shows that in this context Pharaoh is Esau. So it’s telling us: before that Esau smites Gaza. Have we seen in the news the white man has smitten Gaza today? The answer is yes.

“Behold, waters rise up out of the north”: Jeremiah 46:7 shows the waters are nations. This goes with the same thing we just read in Isaiah 14 about the north. “And shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all that is therein; the city, and them that dwell therein: then the men shall cry”: we see that in Gaza. “And all the inhabitants of the land shall howl.”

“At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong horses”: weapons of war, tanks and chariots. “At the rushing of his chariots, and at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands”: they have no power in Gaza to help their children. You see in the news sons and daughters dead, and the people of Gaza have no power, no strength to do nothing.

“Because of the day that cometh to spoil all the Philistines”: the Palestinians. “And to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon”: write this down, brothers, Lebanon. Didn’t they just strike Lebanon? They said Hezbollah shot missiles from Lebanon, and Israel shot missiles over there too.

“Every helper that remaineth”: that’s their terror groups, that’s Hamas, that’s Hezbollah, those are their helpers.

“The remnant of the country of Caphtor”: that’s the same land, Palestine.

“Baldness is come upon Gaza”: they’re wiping Gaza out, buildings being crushed and destroyed. “Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley”.

“How long wilt thou cut thyself?” Pay close attention: that’s the Shiite Muslims. They perform a ritual where they cut themselves. All the Muslims don’t do it, but the Shiites do. How long will you cut yourselves?

“O thou sword of the Lord, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still.” The sword of the Lord is talking about the white man, the wicked: Psalms 17:13 calls the wicked God’s sword.

“How can it be quiet, seeing the Lord hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore?” How can the sword of the Lord be quiet? The Lord gave them a charge. The seashore, brothers, is Gaza, along the Mediterranean. “There hath he appointed it.” Prophecies upon prophecies upon prophecies.

precepts.why:
For those who say these scriptures already happened once: “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” A ring goes round and round and round. The judgments don’t stop; they keep going and going.

Many of the people of those lands got moved out, but the judgment still sits for that land. There is no slackness of the last judgments on the people of the land, and no swiftness of the first either. God’s judgment keeps on going: it takes a licking and keeps on ticking.

So Jeremiah’s word against the Philistines and Gaza is coming to pass again today.

Who is the Pharaoh of today? “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh”, “have I raised thee up”. Why was Paul talking about Pharaoh? Read from verse 13: “As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” Jacob includes Paul and the rest of the Israelites. And who was Esau in the time of Paul, brothers? Rome.

“What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God?” Is God unrighteous because he loves Jacob and hates Esau? “God forbid”: the answer is no.

“For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.” Pay close attention: Paul is comparing Jacob and Esau to Jacob and Pharaoh back in the day, the Egyptians. The compassion is on Israel; he’s having compassion on us.

“So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.” You can’t will yourself to be the people of God, you can’t fake yourself to be the people of God, and you can’t steal the land of God to be the people of God.

Now we know who Pharaoh is in this context: it’s Esau. It was Rome at the time; it’s Esau. “That I might shew my power in thee”: that’s why Esau today is the world’s superpower. America is the world’s superpower on this side, and Israel is a superpower over there in the Middle East. So the Pharaoh that smites Gaza is Esau, the white man.

What does it mean, waters rise up? “Who is this that cometh up as a flood, whose waters are moved as the rivers?” It’s talking about nations.

So the “waters” that “rise up out of the north” and overflow the land of the Philistines are nations coming out of the north.

“Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”. The wicked, which is thy sword: this white man is the wicked, and they are God’s sword on the earth.

So “O thou sword of the Lord” in Jeremiah 47 is the white man, the wicked, given a charge against Ashkelon and against the seashore, Gaza.

What about Lebanon? We just read that they would cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper. “For the violence of Lebanon shall cover thee, and the spoil of beasts, which made them afraid, because of men’s blood, and for the violence of the land”. What land is it talking about? Lebanon.

The violence ain’t going to stop, brothers; it’s going to be like a woman in travail. These Arab nations are going to gather themselves together against the so-called Israel of today.

sense.text:
“The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof”: write this down, brothers, Syria. Hadrach and Damascus is modern-day Syria.

“When the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the Lord”: everybody wants to know what the Lord is going to do. Everybody on the planet is going to know that all of this that’s going on is of the Lord: what is the Lord going to do next?

“And Hamath also shall border thereby”: write this down, Hamath is Syria. “Tyrus, and Zidon”: now bear with me, brothers. This Tyrus and Zidon is not Lebanon. It took a while to figure this one out, but this one is not Lebanon. “Though it be very wise”: that’s not Lebanon.

Who is this talking about, brothers? Esau, Edom.

“And Tyrus did build herself a strong hold”: a strong hold is like a military base. That’s not Lebanon. “And heaped up silver as the dust, and fine gold as the mire of the streets”: that means they’re wealthy and rich. That’s not Lebanon; Lebanon today is like a third-world country.

So who is this Tyrus and Zidon that is so wise, that has the strong military base, and is wealthy beyond belief, heaping up silver and gold as dust? Who’s got a military base, brothers? Who’s the wealthiest people on the earth? Esau, Edom, the white man, particularly America.

“Behold, the Lord will cast her out, and he will smite her power in the sea”: he’s going to destroy their navy, their Marines. All that power you’ve got in the sea, God said, I’m going to destroy it. “And she shall be devoured with fire.”

“Ashkelon shall see it, and fear”: Ashkelon, which is in Israel, shall see it and fear. Why? Because America is coming to help. America sends their navies and their Marines to help, and Ashkelon is going to see the navy destroyed and the Marines destroyed.

“Gaza also shall see it, and be very sorrowful”: that proves the white man has taken over Gaza 100%, because America is not coming to help the Palestinians. He’s coming to help the white man and the Israelis.

“And the king shall perish from Gaza”: they just killed their leader; they’re going to kill a leader. “And Ashkelon shall not be inhabited.”
“And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod”: people use that word, and it’s in the Bible. That’s what God says. “And I will cut off the pride of the Philistines”: the pride of the Palestinians.

“But he that remaineth”: it’s talking about the Israelites that remain. “Even he, shall be for our God”: we shall be for the Lord. “And he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite”: Ekron as a Jebusite means a slave, a servant.

“And I will encamp about mine house because of the army”: God is going to encamp around his house because of the armies of the nations. “And no oppressor shall pass through them any more”: no oppressor shall pass through us any more. “For now have I seen with mine eyes”: God is looking upon us for good and not bad, for blessings and not curses.

precepts.why:
Who is this Tyrus that is so wise, with the strong hold and the silver and gold? Here’s a precept: “Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus, Thus saith the Lord God; Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God”. That’s not Lebanon. What people say they are God today, brothers? The white man.

“I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas”: they have a military base, a navy, in the seas. That ain’t Lebanon; that’s the so-called white man, particularly America. “Yet thou art a man, and not God”: you are a man, you’re not God, “though thou set thine heart as the heart of God”.

“Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”: they’ve got the greatest technology. America has the greatest technology, and they have shared it with the so-called Israelis and with Britain as well.

“With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures”: they got wealthy beyond belief. “By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches”.

So the Tyrus of Zechariah 9 that is “very wise”, that built “a strong hold” and “heaped up silver as the dust”, is Esau, Edom, the white man, particularly America.

sense.text: “Thus saith the Lord God to Tyrus”: Tyrus again, brothers. This is the so-called white man, America. “Shall not the isles shake at the sound of thy fall, when the wounded cry, when the slaughter is made in the midst of thee?”

“Then all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and lay away their robes, and put off their broidered garments: they shall clothe themselves with trembling”: the nations shall clothe themselves with trembling. “They shall sit upon the ground, and shall tremble at every moment, and be astonished at thee.” When the nations see Tyrus fall, and Tyrus is a parable, a metaphor for America, they’re going to lament, they’re going to cry, they’re going to tremble.

“And they shall take up a lamentation for thee, and say to thee, How art thou destroyed”. Remember, in Revelation it said Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen. It’s talking about the same thing. The lamentation is the great weeping and mourning we read about in Revelation 18.

“The renowned city”: Revelation 17:18 shows that renowned city is the great city that reigns over the kings of the earth, Babylon the great, the United States of America.

“Which wast strong in the sea”: they have military bases everywhere, navies and Marines in the sea. “She and her inhabitants, which cause their terror to be on all that haunt it”: Jeremiah 49:16 and Isaiah 14:4-6 are examples of their terror.
“Now shall the isles tremble in the day of thy fall”: everybody is going to tremble when America falls. “Yea, the isles that are in the sea shall be troubled at thy departure.”
“When I shall make thee a desolate city, like the cities that are not inhabited; when I shall bring up the deep upon thee”: the nations. “And great waters shall cover thee”.

“When I shall bring thee down with them that descend into the pit, with the people of old time”: just like the people of old time. “That thou be not inhabited”: Babylon, America, shall not be inhabited no more.

“And I shall set glory in the land of the living”: Revelation 21:23 shows the glory in the land of the living is the kingdom of heaven on earth, New Jerusalem.

“I will make thee a terror”: the Lord says, I will make thee a terror on this earth. “And thou shalt be no more”: the Lord is going to make sure she’s destroyed. “Though thou be sought for, yet shalt thou never be found again”: though nations seek for her. That’s utter destruction upon Babylon, which is called Tyrus here in this chapter.

precepts.why:
For “the renowned city”: “And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.” That woman is Babylon the great, the United States of America. That’s the one that rules over the kings of the earth.

So the renowned city of Tyrus that the nations lament over is America.

“Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” See, John called it Babylon, Ezekiel calls it Tyrus, but it’s the same thing.

“And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her”: that’s the great lamentation we read about in Ezekiel. “For no man buyeth their merchandise any more”: the merchandise of gold.

So the lamentation taken up for Tyrus in Ezekiel 26:17 is the great weeping and mourning over Babylon, America, when she falls.

An example of the terror that Tyrus causes “to be on all that haunt it”: “Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”. Who is that talking about, brothers? Esau, Edom. “That holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the Lord.”

“Also Edom shall be a desolation”: in case you didn’t know it’s talking about Edom, it tells you right there. “Every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.”

“As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the Lord, no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.” Just like Sodom and Gomorrah was destroyed by thermonuclear fire, so shall Edom, so shall America.

Another precept of the terror they cause: “That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!”

“The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers. He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger”.

That is the terror of Babylon, America, on all that haunt it: smiting the people in wrath and ruling the nations in anger, until the Lord breaks the staff of the wicked and the nations take up the lamentation, how art thou destroyed.

What is the glory in the land of the living? “For the glory of God did lighten it”: the city that had no need of the sun or the moon to shine in it.

So when Tyrus, Babylon, America, is brought down to the pit, the glory God sets in the land of the living is the kingdom of heaven on earth, New Jerusalem.

sense.text: “Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east”. Where is this vision coming from? From the East.

“Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots”: so who are we prophesying about? The Arab nations.

“And the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth”. Notice it says the multitude of them. This is why they’re all proclaiming, all you Arab nations gather yourselves against Israel. That’s what you’re seeing in the news right now. That’s what they call a holy war, the Jihad: that’s what this is talking about, “that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.”

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath”: the Carmanians is Iran, modern-day Iran. They’re going to go forth “as the wild boars of the wood”, “and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them”: they’re going to join battle with the Arabs.

“And shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians”. What is the land of the Assyrians here in this metaphor? Israel, modern-day Israel.

“And then shall the dragons have the upper hand”. Go back to verse 29 so we know who the dragons are: “the nations of the dragons of Arabia.” So then shall the Arabs have the upper hand, because they’re going to unite.

“Remembering their nature”: they’re going to remember their nature. “Conspiring together in great power to persecute them”: they shall conspire together, and the them they’re going to persecute is the Israelis. We’re reading Bible prophecy.
“And keep silence through their power”: the Israelis are going to be quiet. “And shall flee”: they’re going to flee.

“And from the land of the Assyrians shall the enemy” come against them: they’re going to take the land. “And consume some of them”: they’re going to consume some of them, “and in their host shall be fear and dread, and strife among their kings”: strife among their leaders.

precepts.why:
This is for the dummies out there that got so much to say. Many times the prophecies have occurred, but they are recurring again and again, and here’s the proof, here’s the evidence. The Lord likens his judgment to a ring: “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.”

These judgments are like a ring. They occur like a ring, going around and around: as it was in the first, it shall be in these last days. So the vision from the East is not only something old; it is coming around again now.

Give me that nature. Talking about an Abrahamic peace accord? What are you talking about: they’re going to remember their nature. The angel of the Lord told her she would bear a son and call his name Ishmael, “and he will be a wild man”. That’s his nature, he shall be a wild man. How wild they are: so dedicated to their cause, to their holy war, they will strap C4 to their chest and blow up everybody in the town. They will put bombs on a car, drive to a gate and blow up a whole city if they can.

“His hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him”: they ain’t going to have no friends, so they’re going to come together. It’s what they call today nationalism: all the Islamic nations, the Arabs, will unite as one. So what’s wrong with you black men and Latin men? The white man’s doing it. The Palestinians said, how come Israel has the full support of America and NATO, but the Arab nations sit back and do nothing? Where is your nationalism, where is your unity, where’s your solidarity?

“And he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren”: all his brethren, the 12 princes that Ishmael had, which is all in what they call the Middle East of today. It’s really the East, because there ain’t no such thing in the middle. That is the nature the dragons of Arabia will remember when they get the upper hand.

sense.text: “And the sixth angel poured out his vial upon the great river Euphrates”: the river Euphrates goes from Syria down to Iran and Iraq. “And the water thereof was dried up, that the way of the kings of the east might be prepared.” The kings of the what? The kings of the East. Didn’t we just read in 2 Esdras 15 about a horrible vision in the East, where the dragons of Arabia come out? So the kings of the East also include Arabia and Iran and Iraq.

“And I saw three unclean spirits like frogs come out of the mouth of the dragon”: write this down, politics comes out of the mouth of the dragon. “And out of the mouth of the beast”: economics, their financial policies. That’s NATO, that’s the EU, the European Union, the financial system. “And out of the mouth of the false prophet”: their religion, Christianity.

Those are the three reasons why nations war: politics, money and religion.

“For they are the spirits of devils”. The spirits of what? Devils. Democracy is the spirit of devils, the EU financial system is the spirit of devils, Christianity is the spirit of devils. What are we reading? The Bible.

“Working miracles, which go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle” of the great day of God Almighty. There’s a purpose: to gather them together for the great day of God Almighty.

“Behold, I come as a thief.” Christ said it. Brothers and sisters, watch what’s going on in this earth according to the word of God, according to God’s counsel. Blessed is he that “keepeth his garments”: keep your garments means keep those commandments as Israelites.

“Lest he walk naked, and they see his shame”: that’s talking about sin.

“And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon.” He gathers the nations into Armageddon; that’s where all the nations are going to be gathered. That goes back to Joel 3 about the valley of Jehoshaphat: it’s talking about the same thing, and it’s going to be a great destruction.

precepts.why:
Here’s the precept for being naked and shame. “When Moses saw that the people were naked”, “Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies”, because they were worshipping a golden calf.

So when it’s talking about you being naked and they see your shame, it’s talking about sin: breaking God’s commandments. To keep your garments is to keep the commandments, so you’re not found naked when Christ comes as a thief.

sense.text:
We might think we’re going to get out of this scot-free. Brothers, we ain’t getting out of this scot-free. Brothers and sisters online might ask, well, where do we fit in? Tribulation is coming. You think we’re rising up and Amalek, these so-called Israelis, don’t see us prophesying what is to come? They see the sons and daughters of God waking up, and they’re making laws, making policies against this truth.

“Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly”. Brothers and sisters, you better get yourselves acclimated to fasting, accustomed to fasting.

“Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children”, even the ones still at the breast. “Let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet”: let the bridegroom come out of those weddings you have. Y’all better come take part in this fast. Ain’t no time to celebrate, because it’s tribulation time.

“Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar”: weep between heaven and earth. “And let them say”: this is what we’re going to say in these prayers: “Spare thy people, O Lord”. Why? Because of tribulation. You think war is going to go on across the world and we ain’t going to get touched here? We’re going to get touched here. We’re going to cry, we’re going to weep to the Lord and ask the Lord to spare, because a lot of us are going to die.

Don’t give us to reproach, O Lord, “that the heathen should rule over them”: the heathen, America and Israel, ruling over us. “Wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?” Look, we’ve killed them, we’ve imprisoned them, where is their God? So in our prayers we’re going to say, spare our people, O Lord, don’t give us to reproach to them.

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” It’s worded like that because God’s people are not in the land. God’s people, the elect, are not in the land: we’re over here in America, we’re over in Britain.

“Yea, the Lord will answer and say unto his people, Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith”: blessings and blessings and blessings. Don’t worry, you’re going to be comforted, you’re going to be satisfied.

While brothers and sisters are getting killed and dying in prison, what are we praying for? Not only for us to be spared, but for vengeance. “And I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen”.

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army”: that’s the militaries of the United States of America. God’s going to make something happen where they have to back up from off of us.

He will drive him “into a land barren and desolate”: that’s what they call the Middle East, Israel today. His face toward “the east sea” is the Dead Sea, and “his hinder part toward the utmost sea” is the Mediterranean Sea. “And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up”: destruction, destruction, destruction. Why? Because he has “done great things”.

precepts.why:
Peep this. Christ said, “I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?”

So many of us are going to be getting killed and imprisoned that some brothers and sisters might lose faith: the Lord ain’t with us, why are we dying, why are we getting imprisoned? That’s why Christ asked whether he shall find faith on the earth when he returns. The vengeance we pray for will come speedily, but we have to keep the faith through the tribulation.

sense.text: “Gather yourselves together”: God is commanding us. He ain’t got no time for you as individuals. “Yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: we are the nation not desired. So God commanded us to understand solidarity, to understand unity.

“Before the decree bring forth”: before God’s decree brings forth, meaning before destruction comes, you all better gather yourselves together. “Before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you”. Why will it come upon you? Because we don’t want to gather together: I want to be an individual, I don’t want to be around y’all. The fierce anger of the Lord shall come upon you, “before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth”: that’s us, brothers and sisters, the Israelites, we’re the meek of the earth. “Which have wrought his judgment” means which have kept his commandments. “Seek righteousness”. “Seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.”

Watch this: “For Gaza shall be forsaken”. It’s going to be destroyed. “And Ashkelon a desolation”: Ashkelon, which is in Israel today, shall be a desolation. God is telling you when the destruction comes: “at the noon day”. “And Ekron shall be rooted up”.

The inhabitants of the sea coast: the sea coast is Gaza, and the nation named there was their ancient name, the Palestinians. “The word of the Lord is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines”: the land of the Palestinians. “I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant.”

Peep what it’s saying: the bottom of verse 5 says “I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant”, then verse 6 says “the sea coast shall be dwellings and cottages for shepherds, and folds for flocks.” Let’s see who is going to dwell there.

“And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah”. Who? The remnant of the house of Judah. “They shall feed thereupon”: we’re going to feed there. So one moment there’s going to be nobody there, and the next minute Judah is going to be there.

“In the houses of Ashkelon shall they lie down in the evening: for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.” So Israel: unity, unity, unity. Never give up.
